![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/d2af19519312ad53c09acb57-prompt.png)

The quarter-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=3$ and $b=2.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the parameter angle on the unit circle with coordinates $(x/a,y/b)$. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/d2af19519312ad53c09acb57-solution.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\frac{\pi }{2}]$, we get the quarter-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the quarter-ellipse are 

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/129bcf91ea3b97f7b04b1b99-prompt.png)

The semi-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=2$ and $b=4.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a semi-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the parameter angle on the unit circle with coordinates $(x/a,y/b)$. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/129bcf91ea3b97f7b04b1b99-solution.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\pi ]$, we get the semi-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the semi-ellipse are 

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\pi ].
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +h,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, the ellipse is centered at the point $(3,1),$ $a=2$ and $b=3.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +3,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +1,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the parameter angle on the unit circle with coordinates $((x-h)/a,(y-k)/b)$.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186152190/plots/bdbb9a8da65738153440425a-solution.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\frac{\pi }{2}]$, we get the quarter-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the quarter-ellipse are 

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +3,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +1,\,\theta \in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$
